topic.title: Tense Review in Narratives
topic.summary: Narratives combine past simple for main events with past continuous and past perfect for background and earlier events.

rules.title: Narrative tense sequence
rules.explanation: Use past simple for completed main events, past continuous for an action in progress, and past perfect for an earlier past event.
rules.example: I was walking home when I saw that I had lost my keys.

rules.title: Past perfect in narratives
rules.explanation: Use had plus a past participle to show that one past event happened before another past reference point.
rules.example: The train had left before we reached the station.

topic.title: Past Perfect Continuous
topic.summary: The past perfect continuous describes an activity that continued up to a past time, often emphasizing duration or a visible result.

rules.title: Past perfect continuous form
rules.explanation: Form the past perfect continuous with had been and the -ing form of the verb.

rules.title: Duration before a past point
rules.explanation: Use the past perfect continuous for an ongoing activity that happened before another past event.

topic.title: Future Continuous and Future Perfect
topic.summary: Future continuous describes an activity in progress at a future time; future perfect describes an action completed before that time.

rules.title: Future continuous form
rules.explanation: Use will be plus the -ing form for an action that will be in progress at a stated future time.
rules.example: At eight tomorrow, I will be flying home.

rules.title: Future perfect form
rules.explanation: Use will have plus a past participle for an action completed before a future deadline.
rules.example: By Friday, we will have finished the project.

topic.title: Future in the Past
topic.summary: Future-in-the-past forms describe a later event from an earlier viewpoint, using would or was/were going to.

rules.title: Would for future in the past
rules.explanation: Use would plus the base verb to report a future event viewed from a past time.

rules.title: Was or were going to
rules.explanation: Use was or were going to for a past plan or intention, especially when the plan may not happen.
rules.example: I was going to leave, but the phone rang.
